topic: Coarse Canary Shifts Sever Realtime Clinical Feeds
postText:
At 2 AM in emergency triage, a 30-second service blip is not an inconvenience—it halts real-time patient admissions.

Most teams treat zero-downtime deployment as an abrupt router flip between Blue and Green environments. But in mission-critical healthcare systems running persistent WebSocket telemetry and bi-directional HL7 feeds, hard cutovers sever active sessions and corrupt state mid-flight.

In the hospital where I work, we abandoned all-or-nothing cutovers for telemetry-driven canary analysis:

1. Targeted Ring Routing: Ingress routes synthetic probes and internal staff traffic first via custom header matching before shifting patient-facing loads.
2. Automated Metric Analysis: Ingress advances canary weights (1% -> 5% -> 25%) only when Prometheus queries verify p99 latency and error budgets match green baseline. A 0.2% anomaly halts rollout and rolls back within seconds.
3. Graceful Connection Draining: Target pods receive SIGTERM with long drain timeouts, letting live telemetry streams finish naturally instead of truncating vital records.

Zero downtime is not about shipping fast; it is about keeping blast radius near zero.

How do you handle in-flight state and long-lived connections during zero-downtime rollouts in your production stack?
